title: feat(fields): refuse retired field types at every predicate face, loudly
body:
Part of #4914

Implements the maintainer's ruling of 2026-08-18, recorded verbatim as 「4914 B」:

> Export a single **`isRetiredFieldType(t)`** gate from `@object-ui/fields` and place it **ahead of** each of the six live predicate faces (items **4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10**): a retired spelling fires `reportRetiredFieldType` **once** and takes the established disposition, instead of riding the lookup-family paths or silently degrading. This closes the whole class at once (the #4932/#4942 shape).

And it is the shape it is because of the boundary question the ruling answered on record:

> `owner` arriving through a backend-vocabulary normalizer is an **authoring error to refuse loudly**, not legitimate foreign input to tolerate.

## Why a gate and not a deletion

The prior seat's premise-gate measurement (comment 5324769751) falsified this card's original framing, and its findings are the spec here: the six faces are **live, not dead**. The card's "dead" argument proved too much — these predicates equally accept `reference`, `picklist`, `money`, `integer`, `bool`, `datetime_tz`, all of which are outside spec's closed `FieldType` and none of which was ever retired. They are defensive normalizers over an open backend vocabulary.

Mechanical deletion would have traded a **visible contradiction** for a **silent degradation**: the filter picker collapsing to a bare id box, `$expand` quietly stopping so cells show raw FK ids — verbatim the failure mode `RETIRED_FIELD_TYPES`' own docblock says it exists to prevent. The gate keeps the same fallback and adds the half that was missing: **the author is told**, once, with the migration prescription.

## The six faces

| Item | Face | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | `operatorsForFieldType` (components) | the `user` bucket, item for item, `in` included | the unknown-spelling bucket, + one console line |
| 4 | the filter row's value control (components) | the remote person picker, via its own `type === "owner"` conjunct | whatever an unrecognised spelling draws |
| 6 | `deriveHighlightFields` (plugin-detail) | highlight-friendly — a pill on the strip | refused a slot |
| 7 | `normalizeFieldType` (plugin-view) | `'select'`, same as `picklist` | `'text'`, same as an unknown spelling |
| 8 | `computeLookupExpand` (plugin-dashboard) | actively requested `$expand` | not expanded |
| 9 | `isLookupType` (plugin-dashboard) | `true`, level with `reference` | `false` |
| 10 | `UserFilters`' lookup-like control (plugin-list) | the remote person picker | the ordinary control; the chip still renders |

Each face reads the retirement **table**, never a literal — so the next retirement closes all seven consumers on the day it lands.

### One thing the ruling did not anticipate, and how it is handled

The ruling names `@object-ui/fields` as the gate's home. **`@object-ui/components` is one of the six consumers, and `@object-ui/fields` depends on `@object-ui/components`** (54 source files import from it) — so a `components → fields` import is a package cycle, and a shared table could not live in `fields`.

A second copy inside `components` was the obvious alternative and is exactly wrong: two tables means two `reportedRetiredTypes` sets, so one spelling logs **twice** — the ruling's "fires once" clause would have been false on the day it landed.

So `RETIRED_FIELD_TYPES`, `reportRetiredFieldType`, `resetRetiredFieldTypeReports` and the new gate are homed in `@object-ui/core` (which imports only `@object-ui/types`, and already owns the sibling cross-package field-type vocabulary `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES`) and **re-exported from `@object-ui/fields`**. The ruling's literal requirement holds — `import { isRetiredFieldType } from '@object-ui/fields'` resolves, and is pinned as a test. **No package gained a new dependency**; all seven already carried `@object-ui/core`.

`packages/fields/src/FieldEditWidget.tsx`'s local `isRetiredFieldType` (added by #4942) is deleted, not kept in sync — it was the precedent for the shape, and is now the same function object the other six faces call. That is what makes "a single gate" true rather than aspirational.

## Fixtures — inverted in this same change, never ahead of it

- **Item 12** (`list-offered-operator-expressible-parity.test.ts`) — the retired spelling leaves `PROBE_FIELD_TYPES` (it is not a bucket representative any more) and gains its own inverted describe: it gets the unknown-spelling offering, not the relational one, and everything still offered for it survives the same round trip every other offered id does.
- **Item 14** (`filter-builder-field-switch-value.test.tsx`) — it leaves the "text-shaped families" list and gains a two-part pin: **refused** the relational bucket, and **never eaten** — `retypeFilterValue` is deliberately *not* gated, because a refusal that cleared the row would destroy a stored filter value on the way to showing the author their prescription.
- **The 16th face** (`filter-builder-lookup-empty-options.test.tsx:95,231`) — the *positive* pin on item 4's conjunct is inverted to require the picker's absence plus one console line. `owner_pending` was that file's **only** pin on the type-driven half of the third conjunct, so a live `assignee_pending` (`type: 'user'`, `options: []`, no `referenceTo`) takes the slot: the inversion moves coverage instead of deleting it.

Items **11 / 15 / 13** are out of scope — already delivered by #4942 / #4932. Item 13's remaining `owner` mentions are explanatory comments recording why the spelling left `ALL_TYPES`; they are archive and are untouched.

## Line drift found on re-verification

Re-verified every site against `origin/main` (`3b147a367`) before editing. Against the card's own base (`1ef236e18`): item 4 has drifted **707/982/1442 → 925/1220/1730**, item 7 **133 → 141**, item 8 **102 → 183**. Items 6, 9, 10, 12, 14 and the 16th face are where the last measurement left them (433 / 34 / 49+505 / 100 / 451 / 95+231). Every named face was present; none had disappeared.

## Evidence

All readings below are at `427cf160f` — the final commit, and the pushed head.

- **Targeted suite** — `Test Files 13 passed (13) / Tests 201 passed (201)`, covering the six new face tests, the three inverted fixtures, and the three pre-existing retirement suites (`owner-retired`, `FieldEditWidget.retiredFieldType`, `InlineFieldInput.retiredFieldType`) that read the table this PR re-homes.
- **Repo-wide build** — `Tasks: 43 successful, 43 total` (`turbo run build --filter='!@object-ui/site'`).
- **Repo-wide type-check** — `Tasks: 81 successful, 81 total`. This is the **dependents direction** a contract change owes, run as a provable superset rather than a hand-picked list: the whole repo minus the docs site contains, by construction, both the dependency closure and the dependent set of every changed package.
- **Repo-wide lint** — `Tasks: 47 successful, 47 total`.
- **Gates** — `check:phantom-deps` "✅ Every in-scope import is declared by the package that publishes it", `check:self-import` "✅ No package names itself inside its own src/", `check:control-bytes` "✅ OK (scanned 4734 tracked text file(s))", `check:lint-coverage` "✅ 46/46 packages linted", `check:type-check-coverage` "✅ 45/46 … 41/41 packages compile their tests", `check:changeset-fixed` ✅, `check:changeset-no-major` ✅, `check:spec-symbols` ✅, `check:esm-specifiers` / `check:i18n-keys` / `check:i18n-drift` / `check:i18n-dead-keys` exit 0.

### Published surface, measured rather than asserted

`dist/` **and every `tsconfig*.tsbuildinfo`** were deleted in both trees before rebuilding (a surviving buildinfo makes composite `tsc` skip emit, which would have made the "after" manifest a copy of the "before"; the script prints `tsbuildinfo left after clean: 0`). Whole-tree `.d.ts` sha256 manifests, `origin/main` vs this branch: **166 → 167 files, exactly four entries move** — `core/dist/index.d.ts`, the new `core/dist/utils/retired-field-types.d.ts`, `fields/dist/field-type-alias.d.ts`, `fields/dist/index.d.ts`. Nothing else in either published tree changed. The content delta on `@object-ui/fields` is **purely additive**: the three existing names survive as re-exports, `isRetiredFieldType` is added.

Reachability was resolved **through the TypeScript checker**, not by grepping a barrel — `export *` and `export type { X } from '…'` both propagate a symbol without restating its shape. A throwaway consumer inside `packages/plugin-dashboard` (which depends on both packages) imported all four names from `@object-ui/fields`, bound each to its expected type, and asserted `typeof gateFromCore` and `typeof gateFromFields` mutually assignable: `tsc --noEmit` exit **0**. The probe carries a negative control (`@ts-expect-error` on a misspelled name) and was itself falsified — making that name resolve produced `error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive.`

### Ablation — 8 legs, direction predicted before each run

Restoration ran under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, every mutation was confirmed on disk by injected/removed occurrence counts, and the tree was verified byte-identical afterwards (`SHA256-MANIFEST-IDENTICAL`, `git status` empty). No rebuild is owed: the root `vitest.config.mts` aliases every `@object-ui/*` specifier to the sibling package's `src/`, so these suites run the source that was mutated — which the redness below demonstrates directly.

| Leg | Gate removed | Predicted | Observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1a | `operatorsForFieldType` | bucket + "once" pins red, controls green | 5 red across 3 files, incl. the item-12 and item-14 inversions |
| 1b | the value control | picker-refusal pins red | 3 red, incl. both 16th-face inversions |
| 2 | `deriveHighlightFields` | both doors red, controls green | 4 red / 2 passed |
| 3 | `normalizeFieldType` | red with `'select'` received | 4 red / 2 passed |
| 4 | `computeLookupExpand` | `$expand` pins red, `isLookupType` green | 3 red / 5 passed |
| 5 | `isLookupType` | its pins red, `$expand` green | 2 red / 6 passed |
| 6 | `UserFilters` | picker returns | 2 red / 4 passed |
| 7 | the **dedupe** (`if (!reported.has(…))`) | every "once" pin red, everywhere | 8 red across all 6 files |

**One void leg, reported rather than quietly retried.** Leg 2's first attempt was rejected by my own on-disk check, which required the removed text's count to drop. That check is invalid for an *additive* mutation: putting `'owner'` back into a list injects a string that **contains** the needle, so the count legitimately stays at 1. The mutation had applied; the instrument was wrong. The check now only demands the drop when the needle is not a substring of the replacement, and leg 2 was re-run under it — the numbers in the table are from that run.

## Out of scope, filed

- **#5692** — `plugin-dashboard` holds two more private copies of the reference-bearing field family (`LOOKUP_TYPES`, and the inline `isLookup` in `computeLookupExpand`) that do not derive from `@object-ui/core`'s `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES`, and are not in a subset relation with it in either direction (`tree` only in core, `reference` only in theirs). This also falsifies #5312's closing claim that `paramToField` was the last such copy. Converting them is a behaviour change in both directions and needs its own call; the gate this PR adds runs *ahead* of both predicates and is unaffected either way.

This PR opens as **`Part of`** rather than with any closing keyword. By my audit every enumerated item on the card is now addressed (1–3 and 5 and 13 by #4932, 11 and 15 by #4942, and 4 / 6–10 / 12 / 14 plus the 16th face here) — but that card carries a multi-round PM ledger and the maintainer ruling this PR implements, so whether it retires is the reviewer's call to make deliberately, not a side effect of this merge.
